_note: Small ASVS-5-LIKE sample for the lab. Chapter numbers and names follow OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 (verify at source). Requirement texts are short paraphrases written for this lab, and 'ref' values are SAMPLE references (<chapter>.S<n>), not official requirement IDs. Import the official CSV with load_csv() to work with real IDs.

requirements.text: Database queries use parameterized queries, an ORM used safely, or equivalent protection; data is never concatenated into query text.
Output is encoded for the context it is written into (HTML body, attribute, JavaScript, URL, CSS).
Operating system commands are not built from user input; if unavoidable, arguments are passed without a shell.
Input is validated against an allowlist of expected type, length, range and format on a trusted service layer.
Business logic limits (quantities, prices, step order) are enforced on the server.
Session cookies set Secure, HttpOnly and an appropriate SameSite value; the __Host- prefix is used where possible.
A Content Security Policy restricts script sources and sets object-src 'none' and base-uri.
Framing by other origins is controlled with CSP frame-ancestors.
API responses set a correct Content-Type, and CORS allows only trusted origins (never a reflected Origin with credentials).
HTTP methods not used by an endpoint are rejected.
Uploaded files are limited in size and type, and stored outside the web root with generated names.
Passwords of at least the policy minimum length are allowed, long passphrases are accepted, and composition rules are not forced.
New passwords are checked against a list of breached or common passwords.
Automated guessing is limited (rate limits, progressive delays or lockout with care for denial of service).
Multi-factor authentication is available, preferring phishing-resistant methods.
A new session token is issued at login, and logout invalidates the session on the server.
Access to each data object is checked against the requesting user (no IDOR/BOLA).
Function-level access control is enforced on the server and denies by default.
Self-contained tokens (such as JWTs) are verified with an allowlisted algorithm and checked for expiry and audience.
The authorization code flow uses PKCE and exact redirect URI matching.
Passwords are stored with an approved slow, salted hash (Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt or PBKDF2 with a suitable work factor).
All traffic uses TLS, and certificate validation is never disabled for outbound calls.
Debug features, default accounts and directory listings are disabled in production.
Secrets are not stored in source code; they come from a secrets manager.
Sensitive responses are not cached (Cache-Control: no-store).
Security events are logged without secrets or session tokens, and error pages do not reveal stack traces.
Logs are protected against tampering and sent to a separate, monitored system.
